analysis.title: Home Depot Inc. (HD): First Take: 3Q26 consensus beat; FY26 guidance updated, Announces leadership changes
key_insights: HD reported adj. 3Q26 EPS of $3.86 on 11/17. That was $0.02 below the GS estimate of $3.88 and $0.02 above FactSet consensus of $3.84. EPS grew +3.3% y/y from $3.74.
Net sales rose +4.9% y/y to $43.398bn, against GS $42.619bn and consensus $42.813bn. The beat was 1.8% versus GS.
Comparable sales rose +2.2% y/y, in line with GS and above the +1.8% consensus. Average ticket rose +3.0% y/y to $93.09 (from +2.8% in 2Q). Transactions fell -0.5% y/y to 392.7mn (from -1.0% in 2Q).
Gross margin fell 64bps y/y to 32.8%, below GS at 33.2% and consensus at 33.0%. Adjusted operating margin fell 28bps y/y to 13.0%, below GS at 13.3% and in line with consensus at 13.0%.
Total operating expenses rose +3.1% y/y to $8.6bn but fell 36bps as a share of sales to 19.7%. Adjusted operating profit rose +2.7% y/y to $5.7bn.

Management updated FY26 guidance. Sales growth is now ~+4.5% (prior +2.5% to +4.5%, consensus +4.2%). Comparable sales are ~+1.4% (prior flat to +2.0%, consensus +1.4%). Adj. EPS growth is ~2.0% (prior ~flat to +4.0%, consensus +2.0%).

FY26 gross margin guidance was trimmed to ~33.0% from 33.1% (consensus 33.1%). Adj. operating margin guidance is ~12.8% (prior 12.8% to 13.0%, consensus 12.8%). Capex is expected at ~2.5% of sales versus 2.2% in FY25.
HD announced leadership changes effective November 23, 2026. Richard McPhail becomes CEO and joins the board, Ann-Marie Campbell becomes President and COO, and Jordan Broggi becomes EVP and CFO.
Inventory grew +5.3% y/y, slower than +8.1% in 2Q26 and +9.6% in 3Q25, and close to sales growth of +4.9%. The payables ratio fell to 47.7% from 50.5% a year earlier.

GS lists the topics it will look for on the call: 4Q and FY27 ticket and transaction expectations, quarter-to-date trends, Pro activity and backlog, housing market and big-ticket trends, SRS and GMS growth and margin, and inventory levels.

GS stays Buy with a 12-month price target of $377, built on downside/base/upside relative P/E multiples of 90%/100%/105%. The stock closed at $347.51 on 11/16, implying 8.5% upside, and was trading slightly down pre-market.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its Buy and $377 target after the 3Q26 print. The target is unchanged from the 18-Aug-26 level in the target price history. Valuation rests on relative P/E multiples of 90%/100%/105%.

earnings_insights: HD 3Q26 adj. EPS $3.86 reported 11/17 vs GS estimate $3.88 and FactSet consensus $3.84. 3Q25 EPS was $3.74.
HD 3Q26 revenue $43.398bn reported 11/17 (+4.9% y/y) vs GS estimate $42.619bn and consensus $42.813bn.
HD 3Q26 comparable sales +2.2% y/y reported vs GS estimate +2.2% and consensus +1.8%. 3Q25 comps were +0.2%.
HD 3Q26 gross margin 32.8% reported vs GS estimate 33.2% and consensus 33.0%. Adjusted operating margin 13.0% reported vs GS estimate 13.3% and consensus 13.0%.
HD 3Q26 operating profit $5,661mn reported vs GS estimate $5,654mn and consensus $5,578mn. Tax rate was 25.0% vs GS estimate 24.0%.

HD FY26 company guidance, updated 11/17: sales growth ~+4.5%, comparable sales ~+1.4%, gross margin ~33.0%, adj. operating margin ~12.8%, adj. EPS growth ~+2.0%. Consensus before the update was +4.2%, +1.4%, 33.1%, 12.8% and +2.0% respectively.
GS estimate for the next quarter, 4Q (Jan-27): EPS $2.77. GS FY ending 1/27E EPS estimate is $15.00 vs $14.69 for FY ending 1/26.
HD inventory growth was +5.3% y/y in 3Q26 vs GS estimate of +5.0%. Share count was 997.0mn vs GS estimate of 995.5mn.
risk_factors: Comparable sales could decelerate if housing turnover fails to recover or macro headwinds weigh on home improvement demand.
HD's valuation could be considered high if the housing market enters a more sustained slowdown.
A deterioration in the pricing environment from increased competition.
Top line and margin pressure from lower-than-expected demand and higher supply chain costs.
